query: Forecast US monthly consumer confidence from a fixed SocioVerse population and point-in-time news/indicator information (target month 2026-06).
method_notes: Real-world anchoring for the ConsumerSim reference showcase. Load-bearing published index levels (Conference Board CCI, UMich ICS) and the macro drivers behind the June-2026 news snapshot (gasoline, CPI, unemployment) are sourced; two modeling references cover the core→Bayesian-expansion design and the five-question survey structure. What could not be pinned to a public value (the raised showcase core_ratio, the as-of information-accrual longitudinal framing) is declared an assumption, not invented.

implementation_refs.title: A Hierarchical Bayesian Nonignorable Nonresponse Model for Multinomial Data from Small Areas (Statistics Canada, Survey Methodology 2002)
implementation_refs.takeaway: Justifies the pipeline's core→expand design: predict a small stratified core, then propagate group-level posterior uncertainty over the multinomial (positive/neutral/negative) responses of the five survey questions to the unsampled majority via a hierarchical Bayesian small-area model. Maps directly to BayesianAggregator.update_and_expand.

implementation_refs.title: University of Michigan — Surveys of Consumers (Index of Consumer Sentiment methodology)
implementation_refs.takeaway: The Index of Consumer Sentiment is built from five component questions spanning personal finances (current & year-ahead), buying conditions for durables, and business conditions (12-month & 5-year) — the same five-question skeleton ConsumerSim scores (current_finance, durable_buying, future_finance, business_12m, business_5y). Confirms the survey-instrument structure the decision model emulates.

facts.claim: Conference Board US Consumer Confidence Index for June 2026 inched up 0.6 points to 91.2 (1985=100), from a downwardly revised 90.6 in May.

source.title: US Consumer Confidence Inched Up in June (Conference Board via PR Newswire)

facts.note: Real-world level the corrected_score output (~90-105 range in the pipeline's index scale) should be read against; the pipeline's own history.csv anchors 2026-05 actual=97.0, consistent with this scale.

facts.claim: Within the June 2026 Conference Board reading, the Present Situation Index fell 3.0 pts to 116.4 while the Expectations Index rose 3.0 pts to 74.4.

source.title: US Consumer Confidence Inched Up in June (Conference Board via PR Newswire)

facts.note: Divergence (present down, expectations up) grounds the 'news-driven forward-looking lift' story: contemporaneous news improves the outlook even as the current-situation read stays soft.

facts.claim: University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment (UMCSENT) for June 2026 was 44.8, down about 26.2% year-over-year; the 1-year inflation expectation (MICH) was 4.8%.

source.title: FRED macro snapshot (UMCSENT, MICH), served via the SocioVerse Event service

facts.note: Independently corroborates the 'rebounding from record lows but still historically weak' framing carried in the pipeline's news.jsonl (Reuters/MSN June headlines).

facts.claim: The rebound continued into July 2026: UMich headline sentiment reached 54.4, with all five index components improving.

source.title: University of Michigan — Surveys of Consumers (July 2026 results)

facts.note: Out-of-target-month datapoint kept as directional validation only — the forecast target is June 2026; July confirms the upward trajectory the June news snapshot was already pricing in.

facts.claim: June 2026 macro backdrop: CPI +3.9% YoY, unemployment 4.2%, retail gasoline (GASREGW) $3.83/gal. Gasoline was easing month-over-month off an earlier-2026 spike even though it sat ~21% above year-ago.

source.title: FRED macro snapshot (CPIAUCSL, UNRATE, GASREGW), served via the SocioVerse Event service

facts.note: Explains why the news snapshot's dominant driver is 'gas prices ease' (a recent-months move) while cost-of-living worries persist (gas still elevated YoY, CPI ~3.9%). The elevated-YoY-vs-easing-MoM tension is preserved, not smoothed away.

assumptions.claim: For the showcase run, prediction.core_ratio is raised above the default 0.10 so the fixed 12-persona pool yields a multi-agent LLM core (rather than the 1-agent core that 0.10×12 would round to). The exact value used is pinned in environment.json provider_args/config_overrides and reported in the run narrative.
assumptions.rationale: The 12-persona reference pool sits in 12 distinct demographic cells; at core_ratio=0.10 the stratified core collapses to a single consumer, which cannot exercise the real-LLM path or the Bayesian expansion meaningfully. core_ratio is an explicit adjustable, config-level parameter (no simulator-code change), so raising it for a demo is artifact-level. Not a published quantity — declared, not sourced.

assumptions.claim: The longitudinal axis is an information-accrual sequence over a single target month (2026-06): the same fixed population is re-forecast at successive as_of cutoffs while June news accumulates (news.jsonl spans 2026-06-12 → 2026-07-01). Each step's information set is the point-in-time-safe subset of news/indicators published on or before that step's as_of.
assumptions.rationale: ConsumerSim is natively a point-in-time monthly forecast (n_steps=1 in the template). To show a genuine panel trajectory without fabricating months of unavailable future data, the demo varies as_of within the month the data actually covers — a real, defensible use of the existing information set. The InformationEnvironmentBuilder already enforces the as_of cutoff, so this is artifact-level (target_months/as_of_dates) with no code change.

assumptions.claim: The pipeline's raw_score/corrected_score output is treated as living on a Conference-Board-style index scale (~90-105 region), not the UMich scale (~45-55 region).
assumptions.rationale: The pipeline's history.csv correction anchor (2026-05 actual=97.0) and the resulting corrected_score (~100) align with the Conference Board CCI level (May 90.6 / June 91.2), not the much lower UMich ICS level (44.8). UMich values are retained as directional trend corroboration only. Inferred from the data files, not stated by the pipeline docs.
